rule.S-1: A series generated from a query must name its time relation, its criteria and the report that renders it. A series generated any other way must carry none of the three.
rule.S-2: Only a series generated from a query filters on liveness, and such a series must say whether it does: leaving it unanswered is not the same as answering no.
rule.S-3: In force at the cut-off is itself the liveness test, so the liveness filter has to be on. Turn it on, or select by publication interval instead.
rule.S-4: Only a series that selects by publication interval has a first interval to start. Give that series a start and leave the field empty on every other; a one-off needs none.
rule.S-5: A weekly cadence needs a cut-off weekday, and no other cadence may carry one.
rule.S-6: A monthly or yearly cadence needs a day of the month, and a yearly one needs a month as well. No other cadence may carry either.
rule.S-7: A series with a cadence needs a nominal time of day for its cut-off, and a series without a cadence may not carry one.
rule.S-8: A series with no cadence has no next issue to create automatically and no sequence to number within. Leave creation manual and numbering set to none.
rule.S-9: Page size, orientation and map thumbnails belong to the report: set all three when a report is named, and none of them when it is not.
rule.S-10: A sort field and its direction are set together or not at all. Name both, or clear both.
rule.S-11: A series must declare at least one language, each of them a language this installation runs, with no blanks and no duplicates.
rule.S-12: Every declared language needs its own text with a non-blank name, and no text may exist for a language the series does not declare.
rule.S-13: A series that messages can cite needs a reference format in every declared language.
rule.S-14: This pattern uses a token outside the available vocabulary. Use only the tokens listed beneath the pattern fields.
rule.S-15: Each language must generate its own file name. Two languages sharing one pattern write to the same path, and only the last one written survives.
rule.S-16: The series id is the import and citation key, and it cannot be changed after the series is created.
rule.S-17: A series cannot be made active while any rule fails, because active is what puts it in the publication picker. Fix the rules listed here and activate again.
rule.S-18: The citation field cannot change once an issue has published: the citations already written live in the field configured at the time, and moving it makes them unfindable.
rule.S-19: A series must belong to a publication category. Pick one; the category is also what decides whether published issues reach the public site.
rule.S-20: The owner domain must carry a readable timezone. The cut-offs of a series with a cadence are read in it, and there is no other source for one.
rule.S-21: A series has to say where its cut-off falls by default, and only a yearly series may be cut off at a period boundary. Everything else is cut off at the release.
rule.S-22: Automatic release is not available yet. Every series releases through the manual gate.
rule.S-23: week, weekTo, year, edition, yearNumber and weekNumber are supplied by the issue being rendered and cannot be typed as report parameters. Remove the row.
rule.S-24: A source series is named exactly when the series is compiled from another one, and a compilation carries neither criteria nor a liveness filter: each source issue decided both at its own cut-off.
rule.S-25: The source must be another series, generated from a query, and not itself a compilation. A series cannot compile itself, and compilations cannot be chained.
rule.D-7: A language carrying a reference format must carry a name as well: without one the whole row is dropped on save, and the format goes with it.
rule.C-1: The criteria are incomplete or malformed: the match mode is required, every criterion needs an operator and at least one non-blank value, and a document may hold at most eight criteria.
rule.C-2: Not in is reserved and not supported yet. Express the selection with the criteria that are available.
rule.C-3: The same kind of criterion appears twice with the same operator. Combined with AND that is either redundant or impossible — merge the values into one row.
rule.C-4: This value does not resolve to anything that exists. Correct it or remove it; a criterion that cannot be looked up silently selects nothing.
rule.C-6: The criteria must be scoped by at least one message series or domain. Without one the query reaches every message series in the installation.
rule.C-7: The criteria document is too large. Reduce the number of values so it stays within the stored limit.
rule.C-8: The criteria document is of a version this installation does not read. Enter the selection again on the criteria tab.
rule.C-9: An area or category must be given by its MRN, not by a numeric id. A numeric id resolves here but does not survive an export.
rule.S-20a: Every publication must belong to a domain — a series, an unscheduled one and a one-off alike. That domain is where it is listed and administered, and it decides which desk may change it.
rule.S-20b: A publication available in selected domains must name at least one. Sharing it with nobody is what "this domain only" says.
